targets.rawSql: SELECT step, run_id, value FROM metrics_raw WHERE name = 'loss_ntp' AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL ORDER BY step
SELECT step, run_id, value FROM metrics_raw WHERE name = 'loss_mtp' AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL ORDER BY step
SELECT step, run_id, value FROM metrics_raw WHERE name = 'lr' AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL ORDER BY step
SELECT step, run_id, value FROM metrics_raw WHERE name = 'tokens_per_second' AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL ORDER BY step
SELECT step, run_id, value FROM metrics_raw WHERE name = 'gpu_alloc_gib' AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL ORDER BY step

panels.description: Fraction in [0,1]. Empty until a run that logs model_flops_utilization is loaded.

targets.rawSql: SELECT step, run_id, value FROM metrics_raw WHERE name = 'model_flops_utilization' AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL ORDER BY step

panels.title: Model FLOPs utilization (MFU)

panels.description: Held-out validation loss (validation_loss, nats per scored token) at each validation run, as points, with the training loss_ntp per step as a thin line for comparison. Read from validation_loss rows (written by metrics_writer.py) or, for G5 train_week2.py's own metrics.jsonl, worked out in the query as val/nll_nats / val/scored_tokens. Both are next-token loss in nats. A gap that keeps growing while loss_ntp falls means overfitting. Compare validation_loss only between runs with the same tokenizer.

targets.rawSql: SELECT x AS step, series, y AS value FROM (SELECT step AS x, concat(run_id, ' ', name) AS series, value AS y FROM metrics_raw WHERE name IN ('validation_loss', 'loss_ntp') AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT step AS x, concat(run_id, ' validation_loss') AS series, sumIf(value, name = 'val/nll_nats') / sumIf(value, name = 'val/scored_tokens') AS y FROM metrics_raw WHERE name IN ('val/nll_nats', 'val/scored_tokens') AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL GROUP BY run_id, step HAVING countIf(name = 'val/nll_nats') = 1 AND countIf(name = 'val/scored_tokens') = 1 AND sumIf(value, name = 'val/scored_tokens') > 0) ORDER BY step, series

panels.title: Validation loss (validation_loss, with loss_ntp)

panels.description: Pick the bucket size (10 / 100 / 1000 / 10000) with the bucket variable.

targets.rawSql: SELECT step_bucket AS step, run_id, mean AS value FROM metrics_rollup_${bucket} WHERE name = 'loss_ntp' AND run_id IN ($run) ORDER BY step_bucket

panels.title: Loss (next-token), mean per $bucket-step bucket

panels.description: Empty until gpu_sample telemetry is loaded.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time_1s AS time, concat(run_id, ' gpu', toString(rank)) AS series, mean AS value FROM gpu_telemetry_1s WHERE name = 'power_w' AND run_id IN ($run) AND $__timeFilter(time_1s) ORDER BY time_1s

panels.title: GPU power (W)

targets.rawSql: SELECT time_1s AS time, concat(run_id, ' gpu', toString(rank)) AS series, mean AS value FROM gpu_telemetry_1s WHERE name IN ('temp_c','gpu_temp_c') AND run_id IN ($run) AND $__timeFilter(time_1s) ORDER BY time_1s

panels.description: dead_experts_count per optimizer step: routed experts, over all MoE layers, that got less than 0.1 x the uniform share (1 / number of experts) of their layer's picks in the step. 0 is healthy. A count that stays above 0 means the router has stopped using those experts. Worked out by metrics_writer.py from expert_load when the trainer does not log it.

targets.rawSql: SELECT step, run_id, value FROM metrics_raw WHERE name = 'dead_experts_count' AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL ORDER BY step

panels.title: MoE Dead Experts Count (dead_experts_count)

panels.description: expert_utilization_min per optimizer step: the lowest utilization of any routed expert, where utilization is the expert's share of its layer's picks divided by the uniform share (1 / number of experts). 1.0 is a fair share. Below 0.1 the expert counts as dead, so this line falls before dead_experts_count rises: an early warning. Worked out by metrics_writer.py from expert_load.

targets.rawSql: SELECT step, run_id, value FROM metrics_raw WHERE name = 'expert_utilization_min' AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL ORDER BY step

panels.title: MoE Weakest Expert Utilization (expert_utilization_min)

panels.description: dead_experts_by_layer per optimizer step: dead experts (utilization below 0.1) in each MoE layer, one line per layer and run. Shows where the router is collapsing. Worked out by metrics_writer.py from expert_load; the loader stores layer i as dead_experts_by_layer.i.

targets.rawSql: SELECT step, concat(run_id, ' ', replaceOne(name, 'dead_experts_by_layer.', 'layer ')) AS series, value FROM metrics_raw WHERE name LIKE 'dead_experts_by_layer.%' AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL ORDER BY step, series

panels.title: MoE Dead Experts by Layer (dead_experts_by_layer)

panels.description: MoE routing imbalance per optimizer step: the worst MoE layer's (max expert load - mean load) / mean load (DeepSeek MaxVio, per batch). 0 = perfectly balanced; 1.0 = busiest expert gets twice the average share. Computed from expert_load by metrics_writer.py.

targets.rawSql: SELECT step, run_id, value FROM metrics_raw WHERE name = 'router_max_vio' AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL ORDER BY step

panels.title: MoE Router MaxVio (router_max_vio)

panels.description: expert_load_imbalance per optimizer step: busiest expert / average expert, max(load) / mean(load) (= max(shares) x number of experts) in the worst MoE layer. 1.0 = perfectly balanced; 2.0 = the busiest expert gets twice the average share; the number of experts = every pick goes to one expert. Equals router_max_vio + 1 (panel 21). Computed from expert_load by metrics_writer.py.

targets.rawSql: SELECT step, run_id, value FROM metrics_raw WHERE name = 'expert_load_imbalance' AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL ORDER BY step

panels.title: MoE Expert Load Imbalance (expert_load_imbalance)

panels.description: gpu_temp_c per optimizer step (degrees C, rank 0's GPU, from NVML) with gpu_thermal_throttle next to it: 1 when NVML reports HW (0x40) or SW (0x20) thermal slowdown, so the GPU lowered its clocks because of heat. Colours: green below 75 C, yellow from 75 C, red from 85 C. Slower steps with throttle 1 mean heat, not the code. Every GPU at 1 s is in panel 12 (gpu_telemetry_1s).

targets.rawSql: SELECT step, concat(run_id, ' ', name) AS series, value FROM metrics_raw WHERE name IN ('gpu_temp_c', 'gpu_thermal_throttle') AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL ORDER BY step, series

panels.title: GPU temperature and thermal throttle (gpu_temp_c, gpu_thermal_throttle)

panels.description: tokens_per_byte per optimizer step: scored tokens / UTF-8 bytes they encode (padding excluded). One 'all' line per run, plus one line per language slice when the trainer logs tokens_per_byte_by_lang. For runs that do not log tokens_per_byte, 'all' is worked out from train/scored_tokens and train/utf8_bytes (summed over ranks). A step change means a new language mix, a tokenizer swap or unexpected text.

targets.rawSql: SELECT step, concat(run_id, ' ', series) AS series, v AS value FROM (SELECT run_id, step, if(name = 'tokens_per_byte', 'all', replaceOne(name, 'tokens_per_byte_by_lang.', '')) AS series, value AS v FROM metrics_raw WHERE (name = 'tokens_per_byte' OR name LIKE 'tokens_per_byte_by_lang.%') AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT run_id, step, 'all' AS series, sumIf(value, name = 'train/scored_tokens') / sumIf(value, name = 'train/utf8_bytes') AS v FROM metrics_raw WHERE name IN ('train/scored_tokens', 'train/utf8_bytes') AND run_id IN ($run) AND run_id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT run_id FROM metrics_raw WHERE name = 'tokens_per_byte' AND run_id IN ($run)) GROUP BY run_id, step HAVING sumIf(value, name = 'train/utf8_bytes') > 0) ORDER BY step, series

panels.title: Tokens per byte (tokens_per_byte, all and by language)

panels.description: Per-step data loader wait time in seconds

targets.rawSql: SELECT step, run_id, value FROM metrics_raw WHERE name = 'loader_wait_time' AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL ORDER BY step

panels.title: Loader Wait Time (s)

panels.description: gradient_norm per optimizer step: the L2 norm of all gradients before clipping (the return value of clip_grad_norm_ in teams/05-architecture/harness/train.py and train_week2.py). The dashed red line is run.grad_clip = 1.0, the value in all Team 5 configs. Above the line, the trainer scales the gradients down on that step. A sudden spike often comes before a loss spike.

targets.rawSql: SELECT step, run_id, value FROM metrics_raw WHERE name = 'gradient_norm' AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL ORDER BY step

panels.title: Gradient norm (gradient_norm, before clipping)

panels.description: Share of steps where clip_grad_norm_ scaled the gradients down (gradient_clipping_applied = 1, gradient_norm > run.grad_clip), as the mean of the 0/1 flag per $bucket-step bucket, plotted at the bucket start. Yellow from 0.5: clipping on most steps may mean the threshold is too low or training is unstable. gradient_norm itself has its own panel.

targets.rawSql: SELECT x AS step, series, y AS value FROM (SELECT intDiv(step, $bucket) * $bucket AS x, concat(run_id, ' clipped share') AS series, avg(value) AS y FROM metrics_raw WHERE name = 'gradient_clipping_applied' AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL GROUP BY run_id, x) ORDER BY step, series

panels.title: Gradient clipping rate (gradient_clipping_applied)

panels.description: update_weight_ratio per logged optimizer step: global L2 update-to-weight ratio ||lr * update||_2 / ||W||_2 (one scalar for the whole model). Equals ||ΔW||_2 / ||W||_2 when update is the parameter change. Very large values may mean unstable steps; near-zero may mean learning has stalled. Worked out by metrics_logger/metrics_writer.py compute_update_weight_ratio (default every 10 steps).

targets.rawSql: SELECT step, run_id, value FROM metrics_raw WHERE name = 'update_weight_ratio' AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL ORDER BY step

panels.title: Update-to-weight ratio (update_weight_ratio)

panels.description: Held-out bits per UTF-8 byte (validation_bpb) at each validation run, one line of points per run. It counts bytes, not tokens, so runs with different G3 tokenizers can be compared on this axis (validation_loss, panel 20, cannot). Lower is better. Read from validation_bpb rows (written by metrics_writer.py); for G5 train_week2.py's own metrics.jsonl, from val/bpb, or worked out in the query as val/nll_nats / (log(2) * val/utf8_bytes). One value per run and step, in that order.

targets.rawSql: SELECT x AS step, series, y AS value FROM (SELECT step AS x, concat(run_id, ' validation_bpb') AS series, multiIf(countIf(name = 'validation_bpb') > 0, anyIf(value, name = 'validation_bpb'), countIf(name = 'val/bpb') > 0, anyIf(value, name = 'val/bpb'), countIf(name = 'val/nll_nats') = 1 AND countIf(name = 'val/utf8_bytes') = 1 AND sumIf(value, name = 'val/utf8_bytes') > 0, sumIf(value, name = 'val/nll_nats') / (log(2) * sumIf(value, name = 'val/utf8_bytes')), NULL) AS y FROM metrics_raw WHERE name IN ('validation_bpb', 'val/bpb', 'val/nll_nats', 'val/utf8_bytes') AND run_id IN ($run) AND value IS NOT NULL GROUP BY run_id, step) WHERE y IS NOT NULL ORDER BY step, series

panels.title: Validation bits per byte (validation_bpb)

panels.description: gpu_memory_used: memory in use on the whole GPU by all processes (nvidia-smi memory.used), in bytes, shown as GiB. One line per run and GPU, the largest value in each 10-second window (metric_list_v1.yaml). G6's GpuSampler sends mem_used_mib about once a second; clickhouse/load_jsonl.py and metrics_logger/metrics_writer.py (gpu_memory_used) multiply it by 1,048,576. Panel 6 (gpu_alloc_gib) counts only PyTorch's allocations, so this line is higher: the gap is PyTorch's cache, the CUDA context and other processes. Close to the GPU's total memory means close to out-of-memory.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toStartOfInterval(time_1s, INTERVAL 10 second) AS time, concat(run_id, ' gpu', toString(rank)) AS series, max(max) AS value FROM gpu_telemetry_1s WHERE name = 'gpu_memory_used' AND run_id IN ($run) AND $__timeFilter(time_1s) GROUP BY time, series ORDER BY time

panels.title: GPU memory used (gpu_memory_used)

list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT run_id FROM metrics_raw ORDER BY run_id
list.label: run_id
list.name: run
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT run_id FROM metrics_raw ORDER BY run_id
